claims.text: Service-relevant thermal and mechanical loading causes an initially homogeneous single-phase HEA to develop local compositional fluctuations at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary compositional fluctuations nucleate nanoscale, less-coherent precipitates.
The emergent grain-boundary features reduce intergranular cohesion.
Reduced intergranular cohesion promotes intergranular brittle fracture.
The proposed mechanism is distinct from conventional segregation-driven embrittlement.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is a compositionally complex high-entropy alloy.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi material is homogeneous, single-phase, and has a uniform microstructure.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi material has high toughness.
Prolonged aging at 700–900 °C combined with cyclic or static loading represents the proposed service-simulation intervention.
High stress and elevated temperature promote local diffusion in the HEA.
Elevated temperature and mechanical stress enhance atomic mobility at grain boundaries.
Enhanced grain-boundary mobility facilitates localized compositional fluctuations and nucleation of incoherent or less-coherent precipitates.
The proposed grain-boundary precipitates hinder grain-boundary sliding.
The proposed grain-boundary features accommodate less plastic strain and serve as crack-initiation sites.
Relative to the unaged control, aged and loaded specimens will have reduced ductility and toughness.
Aged and loaded specimens will transition toward intergranular brittle fracture.
Aged and loaded specimens will exhibit new grain-boundary precipitates or segregation patterns.
The as-processed baseline has no detectable grain-boundary precipitates or compositional gradients.
The proposed embrittlement occurs when temperature and stress activate local diffusion but remain below the thresholds for full phase transformation and catastrophic grain coarsening.
The critical temperature-stress-time combination and segregation kinetics have not been quantitatively determined.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis calls the mechanism distinct from conventional segregation-driven embrittlement, but its stated mediator and mechanism are themselves grain-boundary segregation and precipitation. No distinguishing mechanistic feature is specified.
